headline: Review Oregon State Park and National Forest Access Rules
reservation: Access involves multiple jurisdictions; Multnomah Falls often requires a seasonal timed-use permit for the plaza or parking, while other areas require a Northwest Forest Pass or Oregon State Parks permit. Lodging in Hood River or Cascade Locks should be booked months ahead for summer, but does not guarantee parking at popular trailheads. Check the official Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area site for current permit systems.

days.title: Waterfall Corridor and Historic Heights

stops.name: Vista House at Crown Point
stops.detail: Visit this 1918 observatory for a panoramic view of the river corridor before the highway descends into the forest.

stops.name: Multnomah Falls
stops.detail: View the state's tallest waterfall from the bridge or lower plaza; verify if a timed-entry reservation is active for your dates.

stops.name: Latourell Falls
stops.detail: Walk the short path to see the plunge waterfall against a backdrop of distinct columnar basalt formations.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours for scenic road transit and parking delays; conditions vary by season.
days.note: The Historic Columbia River Highway is narrow with frequent pedestrian traffic near trailheads.

days.title: Riverside Culture and Cascade Locks

stops.name: Bonneville Lock and Dam
stops.detail: Explore the visitor center to learn about river navigation and view fish passage galleries during seasonal migrations.

stops.name: Bridge of the Gods
stops.detail: Cross this historic cantilever bridge for views of the river, noting that tolls apply and pedestrian paths are narrow.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers; bridge traffic can vary.
days.note: Check the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers site for current dam visitor facility access status.

days.title: Hood River Orchards and Eastern Sun

stops.name: Hood River Waterfront Park
stops.detail: Watch windsurfers and kiteboarders harness the Gorge winds from the safety of the shoreline path.

stops.name: Rowena Crest Viewpoint
stops.detail: Drive east to this iconic horseshoe curve for a transition into the drier, open plateau landscape.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the loop; eastern Gorge wind can affect high-profile vehicles.
days.note: Summer heat is significantly higher in the eastern Gorge than the western forest corridor.

intel.title: Corridor Parking Limits
intel.text: Parking lots at Multnomah Falls and Latourell Falls often reach capacity by mid-morning on weekends. Use designated spots only to avoid towing in the narrow scenic highway corridor.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable in the deep canyons between Troutdale and Cascade Locks. Download offline maps before leaving gateway towns like Hood River.

intel.title: Town-Based Services
intel.text: Fuel stations are concentrated in Troutdale, Cascade Locks, and Hood River. Ensure your tank is sufficient before exploring the rural fruit loops or eastern viewpoints.

intel.title: Weekday Advantage
intel.text: Visit the Waterfall Corridor on Tuesday or Wednesday to avoid the heaviest regional traffic. Early morning starts are essential for securing parking at trailhead hubs.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Sections of the Historic Columbia River Highway may close for winter weather or maintenance. Check TripCheck Oregon for real-time state highway status.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at PDX and stop in Troutdale for supplies before entering the scenic corridor. Check-in at Hood River is typically mid-afternoon.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the highway; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved forest service roads.
plan.goldenHour: Rowena Crest Viewpoint offers dramatic lighting at sunset; bring layers as wind increases after dusk.
